aiOverview.content: The 2026 ACC/AHA guidelines for managing dyslipidemia (replacing the 2018 guidelines) emphasize earlier, more aggressive LDL-C lowering to reduce cardiovascular risk. Key targets include an LDL-C goal of <100 mg/dL for intermediate-risk individuals, <70 mg/dL for high-risk, and <55 mg/dL for very high-risk atherosclerotic cardiovascular disease (ASCVD) patients. Key Updates in the 2026 Guidelines Treatment Goals Return: The new guidelines reintroduce specific LDL-C and non-HDL-C targets rather than relying solely on percentage reductions. Primary Prevention: Uses the AHA PREVENT-ASCVD equations for risk assessment. PREVENT-ASCVD equations Lower LDL Targets: Patients with ASCVD at very high risk should aim for LDL-C <55 mg/dL. LDL-C 190 mg/dL or Higher: For severe hypercholesterolemia, if LDL-C remains $\ge$100 mg/dL on max statins, addition of ezetimibe is a 2a recommendation. ezetimibe Lipoprotein(a) [Lp(a)]: The guideline recommends measuring Lp(a) at least once in adulthood to assess risk. Lipoprotein(a) Coronary Artery Calcium (CAC) Scoring: Expanded use of noncontrast CAC scans for men >40 and women >45 with borderline or intermediate risk. A CAC score $\ge$100 supports an LDL-C goal <70 mg/dL, and $\ge$300 supports an optional <55 mg/dL. Coronary Artery Calcium (CAC) noncontrast CAC scans Apolipoprotein B (ApoB): Used to assess residual risk, especially in patients with high triglycerides or diabetes. Apolipoprotein B (ApoB) Statin Intensity Recommendations (From 2018/Maintained) Statin Intensity Recommendations High-Intensity Statin ($\ge$50% LDL-C reduction): Atorvastatin 40–80 mg, Rosuvastatin 20–40 mg. Moderate-Intensity Statin (30%–49% reduction): Atorvastatin 10–20 mg, Rosuvastatin 5–10 mg, Simvastatin 20–40 mg. Key Lifestyle & Prevention Steps Lifespan Approach: Treatment decisions start earlier in life, particularly for those with elevated lifetime risk. Diet & Exercise: Emphasis on vegetables, fruits, whole grains, and healthy fats, limiting saturated fats and ultraprocessed foods. ultraprocessed foods Checkups: Regular screening is essential.
